item.title: CIPTA Debuts High-Density AI GPU Servers and Edge Workstations at CloudFest 2026
item.description: Making its European debut at CloudFest 2026, Malaysia-based EMS provider CIPTA, powered by PC chassis veteran InWin, is making a massive entrance into the enterprise AI market. Highlighting Malaysia's rise as a global AI manufacturing hub, CIPTA has unveiled the monstrous 8-GPU RG658 PRO server and the high-availability cubePRO edge workstation.

item.title: US Prosecutors Indict Three Individuals in Alleged AI Chip Export Conspiracy
item.description: U.S. federal prosecutors have indicted three individuals, including a co-founder of server manufacturer Super Micro Computer, on charges related to an alleged conspiracy to violate U.S. export controls. The unsealed indictment accuses the individuals of attempting to divert approximately $2.5 billion worth of restricted Nvidia AI technology to China.

item.description: Whether you're buying a new headset for your gaming setup or booking concert tickets, your personal details are being wrapped in layers of protection you'll never actually see

item.title: How Kie.ai’s Gemini 3 Flash API Fits Gaming Tools, Live Chat, and Player Support
item.description: Gaming tools live or die by responsiveness. A live chat assistant that answers too slowly, a support bot that loses context, or a community tool that struggles during patch-day traffic quickly becomes part of the problem instead of the solution.

item.title: Viral Photo Shows Driver Gaming Mid-Trip as Cabal Anniversary Event Gains Attention
item.description: A quick glance at the dashboard turned into a double take. What looked like a navigation setup was actually a full-on gaming session, right in the middle of traffic. As the photo circulates online, it raises eyebrows and sparks various opinions, all while the Cabal anniversary event continues to draw players in.

item.title: NBI Seizes ₱31.4M in Counterfeit Seagate and Sandisk Storage Devices in Manila
item.description: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has successfully confiscated over ₱31.4 million worth of suspected counterfeit data storage devices in a series of coordinated raids in Manila. The operations targeted establishments allegedly distributing fake high-capacity memory cards and hard drives bearing the trademarks of major brands like SanDisk and Seagate.

item.title: Colorful Announces Intel Core Ultra 200S Plus Support and New 800-Series Motherboards
item.description: Colorful has announced BIOS support for Intel’s Core Ultra 200S Plus processors across its 800-series motherboard lineup. Alongside the update, the company introduced three new models, including the iGame Z890M ULTRA Z, which features a BTF 3.0 back-connect layout and direct-plug power connectors for both the motherboard and GPU.

item.title: Arm Debuts AGI CPU: Their First Physical Product Co-Developed with Meta
item.description: Arm has officially disrupted the data center market by launching the Arm AGI CPU: their first-ever production silicon co-developed with Meta. This shifts Arm from a pure IP licensing model to a merchant silicon provider to customers who want a turnkey silicon they can grab-and-go for their application, Arm’s new 136-core Neoverse V3-based processor is engineered specifically for "agentic AI" workloads, promising over 2x the performance per rack compared to traditional x86 alternatives.

item.title: US FCC Bans New Authorizations for Foreign-Made Consumer Routers Over Security Concerns
item.description: The United States Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has officially added all foreign-produced consumer-grade routers to its Covered List, halting the authorization and import of new models into the US market. While this is a strict US-specific regulatory action, the global implications for networking hardware manufacturers are significant, even as existing and previously authorized models remain unaffected.

item.title: CHUWI Issues Response to Mislabelled CPU Scandal
item.description: Following recent reports of laptops shipping with incorrectly identified processors and a subsequent denunciation from AMD, CHUWI has officially addressed the controversy. The manufacturer attributed the issue to a "production error" affecting a limited number of CoreBook X and CoreBook Plus units, and has initiated a full refund program for affected customers.
